test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Advanced Full Test - 01
subject: general
question: Which of the following functions is NOT typically performed by the High Courts in India?

options.text: Superintending lower courts within the state
Conducting trials for criminal cases as a court of first instance
Issuing writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Conducting trials for criminal cases as a court of first instance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **High Courts** in India do not typically conduct trials for criminal cases as a court of first instance. This function is primarily performed by **lower courts**, such as the Sessions Court.
 
• The role of the High Courts is generally to function as **appellate courts**, reviewing decisions made by subordinate courts.
 
• High Courts have jurisdiction over **constitutional matters**, including issuing writs for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** under Article 226 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They supervise and superintend the functioning of **lower courts** within the state to ensure proper administration of justice.
 
• Criminal cases are usually first handled by **Magistrate Courts** or Sessions Courts, depending on the severity of the crime, and only reach the High Court in appellate or revision cases.
 
• The High Court's powers include **judicial review**, ensuring that laws and actions by the government comply with the Constitution.
